title: Global Sea Surface Currents and Temperature
summary: The ocean's surface temperature, sung by its currents. Geophony.
description: Ocean surface currents swirl around the globe, coloured by sea surface temperature from the ECCO2 ocean model (MIT/JPL) on a 0 to 32 °C colour bar. The lead melody is the global average sea surface temperature, frame by frame: it rises and falls by about 1.4 °C over the movie. Six soft pad voices underneath are the six latitude bands, from the Arctic (lowest notes) to the tropics (highest) and down to Antarctica.

legend.meaning: Global mean sea surface temperature. Higher pitch means warmer. The two-octave range covers 20.3 to 21.7 °C, so small changes are easy to hear.

Average temperature of six latitude bands, 30 degrees each, from 90° North to 90° South. Pitch spans the full colour bar, 0 to 32 °C, so warm tropical bands are high and cold polar bands are low. Each band also sits in its own register, shifted by up to 6 semitones: northern bands a little higher, southern a little lower.
Press A to swap the lead for the same temperatures played in random order. It sounds like a tune but no longer follows the ocean.

band_pitch_map.note: Each band uses this map shifted by its sweep pitch_offset (jukebox.score.mapping.band_voices).

data_source: ECCO2 ocean model (MIT/JPL), as rendered in NASA SVS visualization 3912. Values were recovered from the movie by inverting its 0 to 32 °C colour bar; 42% of pixels matched the colour bar (land, labels and gaps between flow lines are skipped).
